key_insight: Ly and Gong propose that deep learning's unpredictability stems from fractal basin geometry: starting points that lead to different outcomes are interwoven at arbitrarily fine scales. Increasing numerical precision may therefore offer little improvement in predictability.
problem_solved: The paper addresses why deep learning outcomes can remain difficult to predict and reproduce, even when starting conditions are controlled with greater precision.
method: Frame training outcomes in terms of basins: sets of starting points that lead to the same outcome.
Propose fractal boundaries that interweave basins at arbitrarily fine scales.
Connect this geometry to limits on how much greater starting-point precision can improve outcome prediction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the proposed mechanism suggests that tighter numerical precision alone may not ensure reproducibility. It motivates assessing variability across runs rather than relying on a single training outcome.
visual_elements: Color-coded basin map showing nearby starting points leading to different outcomes.
Nested zoom panels illustrating how basin interweaving persists at finer scales.
Conceptual training trajectories showing tiny starting-point differences leading to distinct outcomes.
Conceptual chart contrasting increasing precision with limited gains in predictability.
paper_title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
